newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scor underlying performance solid - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Scor underlying performance solid - analysts.

text.p: French reinsurer Scor's 1996 performance was in line with market expectations and the big difference between its profits reported according to U.S. GAAP accountancy standards and French accounting methods did not detract from a solid underlying performance, analysts said.
"This profit difference doesn't have anything to do with the underlying reinsurance business which looks fine," said one analyst.

The reinsurer's net attributable profit according to French accounting standards jumped 20 percent to 624 million francs from 522 million while according to U.S. GAAP methods, profits were up just 2.2 percent to 705 million francs from 690 million.
Scor shares finished up 1.56 percent at 241.0 francs.

A company official said the difference in the results lay in in the way U.S. and French accounting rules treated capital gains on sale of treasury stock, exchange rate fluctations and equalisation reserves.

For instance, he said, Scor had a capital gain of 29 million francs after tax on sale of treasury stock which it was able to include in its profit and loss account under French rules, but which it had to include in shareholders' equity under U.S. rules.

The official said the fall in return on equity under U.S. GAAP rules to 10.7 percent from 12.8 percent was only a "mechanical decrease". Under French rules, return on equity rose to 11.3 percent from 10.3 percent.
"This reflects the 19.3 percent increase in shareholders' equity to 7.2 billion from 6.04 billion at December 31, 1995," the company said.
U.S. accountancy methods dictated that assets must reflect book value while French rules stipulated they must reflect historic value, the company official said.
Scor began publishing its results according to U.S. GAAP methods ahead of the listing last year of its shares on Wall Street.

The Scor official said the company was obliged under French regulations to issue its results in conformity with French GAAP but that authorities were studying changes to this rule. If permitted, the company would switch to reporting its results only according to U.S. GAAP standards, he said
"If we are authorised, we will do it," he said. "These (U.S. GAAP) are internationally recognised accounting standards."
Analysts said Scor had fared well in 1996 in the face of more difficult market conditions.

"This is a quality player which has shown consistent profits despite a softening in the reinsurance cycle, thanks to the restructuring of their reinsurance portfolio which has been ongoing since 1993," said an analyst.
Analysts said there was no doubt that leaner times for the sector lay ahead.
"It is clear we are past the peak of the reinsurance cycle and it is going to be more difficult over the next year or two," said another analyst.
